title: Web/PWA platform epic
body:
## Context
Web/PWA is one of Sane Notes' five first-class surfaces (locked decision 1) and the most constrained one. The locked stack is Flutter Web — CanvasKit default with automatic JS fallback, skwasm where cross-origin isolation is deployable — positioned as 'view + light-edit + quick capture', per `docs/platform/web.md` and `docs/adr/0010-web-pwa-strategy.md`. Heavy inking is steered to the installed native apps, but the web editor must still meet the ≤ 30 ms Chrome-desktop pen-to-pixel budget (decision 7). This epic is the umbrella for every browser-surface concern and owns the web-specific gates.

## Scope
**In:** coordinating all SN-WEB child issues — dual WASM/JS build, bundle budget, Pointer Events pen path, Chromium wet-ink enhancement, OPFS + SQLite-WASM persistence and eviction guards, PWA plumbing (manifest, service worker, offline, install, file handling, share target, badging), File System Access, web sign-in and Drive/OneDrive sync, the ASVS 5.0 L2 header stack (CSP/Trusted Types/COOP/COEP/SRI), hosting/CDN, keyboard-first navigation, accessibility semantics, the 'try it now' guest flow, and the browser-matrix + perf harness.
**Out:** the shared ink engine, document model, crypto and sync cores — owned by SN-INK/SN-CORE/SN-CRY/SN-SYNC and only integrated on the web surface here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The web app runs on Chrome/Edge 120+, Safari 17+, Firefox 125+ and Samsung Internet per `docs/platform/compatibility-matrix.md` §3.
- [ ] Zero-knowledge holds on web: only ciphertext ever leaves the browser (decision 3).
- [ ] All web gates pass: ≤ 30 ms Chrome-desktop ink, < 3 s cached cold start, Lighthouse PWA installable/offline, ASVS 5.0 L2 headers present.
- [ ] Every child issue below is closed with its own gate green.

## Technical notes
Implements ADR-0010. Child issues:
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-002}} Dual CanvasKit/skwasm build
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-003}} Bundle budget + cold-start gate
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-004}} Pointer Events pen capture
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-005}} Chromium wet-ink fast path
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-006}} Palm rejection + touch-action
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-007}} Safari iPadOS Pencil support
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-008}} OPFS + SQLite-WASM persistence
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-009}} Persistence + eviction guard
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-010}} Manifest + install
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-011}} Service worker offline
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-012}} File handling + share target
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-013}} File System Access
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-014}} CSP + Trusted Types
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-015}} COOP/COEP isolation
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-016}} SRI + baseline headers
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-017}} Hosting + CDN
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-018}} Web sign-in
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-019}} Drive/OneDrive sync
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-020}} Keyboard-first navigation
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-021}} Accessibility semantics + OCR alt-text
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-022}} 'Try it now' guest flow
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-023}} Browser-matrix harness
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-024}} Lighthouse + perf budgets
- [ ] {{SN-WEB-025}} Web handwriting recognition path

## Security & privacy
Aggregates the ASVS 5.0 L2 web posture (decision 8): strict nonce CSP, Trusted Types, COOP/COEP, SRI, TLS-only transport, no note content in logs, ciphertext-only cloud writes. Controls: MASVS-PLATFORM-2, MASVS-STORAGE-1, MASVS-NETWORK-1, MASVS-PRIVACY-1. Web at-rest is a reduced-guarantee posture (no Keychain/Keystore) and is labelled in the privacy dashboard (CLAUDE.md §13 pending decision).

## UX notes
Covers the whole design (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html`, `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md`): Login, Profiles, Onboarding, Library, Editor, Search, Settings and overlays. Everything painted renders in all 17 looks addressed by `(lookId, mode)` and in light + dark; WCAG 2.2 AA and keyboard-first are mandatory on web (decision 10).

## Test plan
Browser matrix in CI ({{SN-WEB-023}}) + Lighthouse/perf ({{SN-WEB-024}}); each child ships its own unit/widget/golden/integration tests under `app/integration_test/` and package tests.

## Dependencies
SN-FND-002 (monorepo scaffold), SN-FND-003 (CI). Children carry their own.

## Definition of done
- [ ] All child issues merged and their gates green
- [ ] Docs/ADR-0010 updated if the web strategy changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Implement dual CanvasKit/skwasm Flutter web build with runtime fallback
body:
## Context
Flutter Web renders only through Skia-on-WASM; the legacy HTML/DOM renderer is gone (`docs/platform/web.md` §2). There are two paths: **CanvasKit** (~1.5 MB WASM, main-thread paint, universal, the only path on iOS browsers) and **skwasm** (~1.1 MB, offloads paint to a Web Worker, but requires **WasmGC + COOP/COEP** cross-origin isolation). skwasm/WasmGC cannot run in any iOS browser (all WebKit), so iPad/iPhone Safari must silently fall back. `flutter build web --wasm` emits **both** and picks skwasm at runtime only where WasmGC + isolation are present, else CanvasKit/JS (needs Flutter 3.24+). This issue stands up that build so the app runs in every supported browser. Implements ADR-0010 decision 1.

## Scope
**In:** wire `flutter build web --wasm` into the dev/beta/release flavours ({{SN-FND-005}}); confirm automatic runtime renderer selection; expose the selected renderer in a redacted diagnostic; pin Flutter stable ≥ 3.24.
**Out:** serving COOP/COEP headers ({{SN-WEB-015}}), the bundle-size CI gate ({{SN-WEB-003}}), the app bootstrap loader UX ({{SN-WEB-003}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `flutter build web --wasm` emits both WASM (skwasm) and JS (CanvasKit) artifacts.
- [ ] On Chrome/Edge 120+ **with** COOP/COEP set, `self.crossOriginIsolated === true` and skwasm engages (paint on a Worker).
- [ ] On iPadOS/iOS Safari 17+, JS/CanvasKit engages automatically and the app renders and takes a note.
- [ ] On Firefox 125+ the app runs on CanvasKit (skwasm treated as (verify)).
- [ ] The active renderer is recorded via `SaneLog` (no PII) and shown in the debug diagnostic; Impeller-not-on-web is documented.

## Technical notes
Configure the `web/` entry and `flutter_bootstrap.js`; drive the flavour via `--dart-define` ({{SN-FND-005}}). Do not hand-force a single renderer — rely on the emitted dual build's runtime fallback. Reference `docs/adr/0010-web-pwa-strategy.md` decision 1 and `docs/platform/compatibility-matrix.md` §3 (renderer-path column).

## Security & privacy
Baseline: keep the Flutter engine current (MASVS-CODE-1); no secrets in build config (`--dart-define`/CI secrets only). Renderer selection must not log any note content.

## UX notes
No visible chrome beyond load, but rendering must be pixel-consistent across both renderers and all 17 looks in light + dark; capture golden parity so a CanvasKit-vs-skwasm difference is caught. Ties into the Editor and Library screens in `design/Sane Notes.dc.html`.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_renderer_fallback_test.dart` (headless Chromium asserts renderer selection and a note round-trip); a golden parity check `app/test/web/renderer_golden_test.dart` on a sample canvas across two looks.

## Dependencies
SN-FND-002, SN-FND-005; SN-INK-009 (spike) informs the tier decision.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR-0010 updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Enforce web bundle-size budget and cold-start gate in CI
body:
## Context
The web build is heavier than a hand-tuned JS app (CanvasKit ~1.5 MB + compiled Dart), which threatens the < 3 s cached-cold-start budget (decision 7, `docs/adr/0010-web-pwa-strategy.md` Consequences). Without a CI budget the bundle silently bloats and first paint regresses on iPad Safari (the JS/CanvasKit path). This task adds a measured initial-download budget and a cold-start smoke check so regressions block merge, and ships the branded bootstrap loader so the first paint is intentional rather than a blank canvas.

## Scope
**In:** a CI step that measures Brotli-compressed initial transfer of the entry chunks and fails over a budget; deferred/lazy-loaded feature chunks (PDF, audio, whisper) split out of the initial payload; a lightweight HTML bootstrap loader (Sane Sage mark placeholder) shown until first frame.
**Out:** production CDN/Brotli serving ({{SN-WEB-017}}), Lighthouse audit wiring ({{SN-WEB-024}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CI fails if the Brotli-compressed initial download exceeds the agreed budget (start: ≤ 3.0 MB initial, documented and adjustable).
- [ ] PDF/audio/whisper code is lazy-loaded and absent from the initial chunk (verified in the manifest).
- [ ] A cached reload cold-starts in < 3 s on the Web-Chrome-desktop reference (measured, recorded per release).
- [ ] The bootstrap loader appears within 500 ms and is removed on first Flutter frame; it renders in light + dark.

## Technical notes
Add a Node/`bash` size check in `.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` (or the web job) reading `build/web` output; use `deferred as` imports for heavy features. Loader lives in `web/index.html` using a single `SaneSageMark` placeholder asset (design rule §9). Reference `docs/platform/performance-budgets.md` and ADR-0010 verify-step 3.

## Security & privacy
Baseline only (MASVS-CODE-1): the loader ships no inline scripts that would need a CSP exception; no secrets; no analytics. No content logged.

## UX notes
Loader matches the Onboarding/Login look in `design/Sane Notes.dc.html`; uses tokens ({{SN-DS-002}}) only, all 17 looks + dark; provides a `Semantics`/`aria` 'Loading Sane Notes' label; respects reduced-motion.

## Test plan
`tools/scripts/web_bundle_budget.mjs` unit-tested on a fixture manifest; `app/integration_test/web_coldstart_test.dart` asserts loader lifecycle; CI artifact records the size number.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002, SN-FND-003.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Wire Flutter web Pointer Events into the sane_ink capture path
body:
## Context
Flutter Web consumes browser **Pointer Events** through the engine and surfaces them to Dart as `PointerEvent`/`Listener` — the **same `sane_ink` capture path** as mobile (`docs/platform/web.md` §3). The rich DOM stylus fields (pressure, `tiltX/tiltY`, `twist`, `altitudeAngle`/`azimuthAngle`) are reached through the engine, not directly, and Flutter has no first-class coalesced-events array (limitation L1/R2). This issue wires the web editor's raw `Listener` onto `sane_ink` capture, feature-detects the stylus fields per event, and adds a `dart:js_interop` shim to read `getCoalescedEvents()` where the engine does not forward high-Hz samples. It is the baseline web-ink path (Tier B) that the ≤ 30 ms Chrome-desktop budget is measured against.

## Scope
**In:** capture via a raw `Listener` (never `GestureDetector`, per CLAUDE.md §8); map `PointerDeviceKind.stylus` pressure/tilt/orientation into `sane_ink` samples; JS-interop coalesced-sample read on secure-context Chromium/Safari 18.2+; velocity-based width when pressure is absent.
**Out:** the Chromium wet-ink low-latency side-canvas ({{SN-WEB-005}}), palm rejection heuristics ({{SN-WEB-006}}), Safari altitude/azimuth specifics ({{SN-WEB-007}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A pen stroke on Chrome desktop captures pressure + tilt and renders through `CustomPainter`/CanvasKit at ≤ 30 ms pen-to-pixel (Tier B gate, decision 7).
- [ ] Coalesced samples are read via JS interop when available and ignored gracefully when not (feature-detected, secure context only).
- [ ] Mouse/finger input still draws with velocity-based width (no pressure) with no thrown errors.
- [ ] No frame > 16.7 ms while writing on the reference desktop; nothing logs ink coordinates in profile/release.

## Technical notes
`plugins/sane_ink_surface` web impl + `packages/sane_ink` capture entry; use `dart:js_interop` for `PointerEvent.getCoalescedEvents()`. Do not enable `GestureBinding.resamplingEnabled` on the draw path. Reference ADR-0008 (ink tiers) and `docs/platform/web.md` §3. Depends on the shared capture from {{SN-INK-002}}.

## Security & privacy
Ink coordinates are content: MUST NOT be logged (MASVS-PRIVACY-1, checklist §7); strokes persist only through the encrypted store (MASVS-STORAGE-1). JS-interop reads only same-origin canvas events; no eval, no third-party script.

## UX notes
Editor canvas screen (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §7.2); the wet stroke must feel immediate. Tokens only; works across all 17 looks + dark. Provide a `Semantics` label on the canvas ('Note canvas'); pen vs finger disambiguation follows `event.kind`.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ink/test/web_pointer_capture_test.dart` (synthetic PointerEvents, pressure/tilt mapping); `app/integration_test/web_ink_latency_test.dart` (Chrome, asserts ≤ 30 ms); golden of a captured stroke.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002, SN-INK-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour changed; perf timeline attached to the PR
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Integrate the Chromium wet-ink fast path into the web app shell
body:
## Context
Flutter owns its canvas, so the lowest-latency web-ink levers — a `desynchronized` 2D/WebGL context and the **Ink API** delegated-trail presenter (`navigator.ink.requestPresenter`) — are not first-class in Dart (R2, `docs/platform/web.md` §3). The ink engine's web path ({{SN-INK-008}}) implements a JS-interop side-canvas that paints the active (wet) stroke ahead of the Flutter frame on Chromium; this issue integrates that path into the web app shell as an **optional progressive enhancement**, gated by capability query, with the Tier B CanvasKit path as the guaranteed fallback everywhere else. It must never block the web release and must degrade invisibly on Safari/Firefox.

## Scope
**In:** capability detection (`getContextAttributes().desynchronized`, `navigator.ink`); a feature flag ({{SN-FND-005}}) to enable/disable the fast path; wiring the wet side-canvas overlay onto the editor and committing finished strokes back into the Flutter/`sane_ink` model; graceful teardown when the presenter is unavailable.
**Out:** the presenter/side-canvas implementation itself ({{SN-INK-008}}), non-Chromium ink ({{SN-WEB-004}} baseline).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On Chrome/Edge desktop the wet-ink overlay engages and measured pen-to-pixel improves versus Tier B (recorded), still ≤ 30 ms.
- [ ] On Safari/Firefox/Samsung the app silently uses the Tier B path with no console errors and no visual seam at stroke commit.
- [ ] Toggling the feature flag off restores the pure-Flutter path with identical stroke geometry.
- [ ] Committed strokes match the wet preview byte-for-byte after flatten; no orphaned overlay pixels remain.

## Technical notes
Use `dart:js_interop` behind `plugins/sane_ink_surface` web; align the overlay canvas to the Flutter view with correct devicePixelRatio and transform. Validate against the SN-INK latency spike ({{SN-INK-009}}). Reference ADR-0008 and ADR-0010 decision 7 (latency levers are future/verify). Progressive enhancement only.

## Security & privacy
Ink coordinates are content — no logging (MASVS-PRIVACY-1). The side-canvas is same-origin, receives no third-party script, and does not weaken CSP (the overlay uses no inline eval). Feature flag defaults per {{SN-FND-005}}, never enabled in a way that changes stored data.

## UX notes
Editor canvas (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §7.2); the enhancement must be imperceptible except as lower latency. All 17 looks + dark unaffected (overlay uses the active brush colour token). No a11y change (canvas Semantics from {{SN-WEB-004}}).

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_wet_ink_test.dart` (Chrome: overlay engages, commit parity); a capability-off test asserting fallback; golden comparing wet-preview vs committed stroke.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-004, SN-INK-008 (and validated by SN-INK-009).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green; perf timeline attached
- [ ] Docs/ADR-0010 updated if the enhancement status changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add palm rejection and touch-action handling to the web canvas
body:
## Context
The browser exposes **no native palm-rejection flag**; on web we must treat `pen` as authoritative and deprioritise concurrent `touch` pointers heuristically (`width`/`height`/`pressure`/`pointerType`), per `docs/platform/web.md` §3. Separately, the canvas must set CSS `touch-action` so browser scroll/zoom does not fight the pen, without permanently blocking user zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). This task adds both so a resting palm and a stylus can coexist on a touchscreen laptop or an iPad in Safari.

## Scope
**In:** a Dart-side palm-rejection heuristic keyed on `PointerDeviceKind` and pointer size; `touch-action: none` scoped to the active drawing region only, re-enabled outside it; a setting to prefer finger-draw when no stylus is present.
**Out:** native low-latency ink ({{SN-WEB-005}}), stylus-extra buttons/hover ({{SN-WEB-007}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] While a `stylus` pointer is active, concurrent `touch` pointers do not create strokes (palm rejected).
- [ ] Page pinch-zoom still works over non-canvas chrome; canvas pan/zoom uses the app's own gesture, not browser zoom.
- [ ] With no stylus connected, finger drawing works (velocity width) and two-finger gestures pan/zoom the canvas.
- [ ] `touch-action` is scoped so accessibility zoom of surrounding UI is never permanently disabled (WCAG 1.4.4).

## Technical notes
Set `touch-action` via the web view host element (JS interop or `HtmlElementView` container); heuristic lives in `packages/sane_ink` capture filter. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §3 palm-rejection row and the input-gestures area. No dependency on native plugins.

## Security & privacy
Baseline (MASVS-PRIVACY-1): pointer coordinates are content and are not logged. No new data flow or egress.

## UX notes
Editor canvas (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §7.2). The behaviour must feel invisible; no toast spam. Honour the Handwriting & stylus settings group (§12) toggle for finger-draw. All 17 looks + dark; keyboard users are unaffected.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ink/test/web_palm_rejection_test.dart` (synthetic simultaneous pen+touch streams); a widget test asserting `touch-action` scope; manual matrix note in {{SN-WEB-023}}.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-004.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Support Apple Pencil on Safari iPadOS web (altitude/azimuth, hover)
body:
## Context
Safari on iPadOS is a Tier 2 web surface that always runs the CanvasKit path (no WasmGC on WebKit) and is where most Apple Pencil web users land. Safari **18.2+** exposes `altitudeAngle`/`azimuthAngle` (cleaner than `tiltX/tiltY`) plus coalesced/predicted events, and Safari 16.1+ supports pointer hover on M-series iPads (`docs/platform/web.md` §3, `compatibility-matrix.md` §3). This issue adapts the web pen path to consume Apple Pencil richness on Safari where present and degrade to tilt or velocity where absent, keeping the experience best-effort but respectable.

## Scope
**In:** feature-detect and map `altitudeAngle`/`azimuthAngle` to brush orientation on Safari 18.2+; consume hover (`onPointerHover`) for a cursor preview; version-gate gracefully to `tiltX/tiltY` on Safari 17.
**Out:** the Chrome Ink API fast path ({{SN-WEB-005}}); native iPad app pencil (owned by SN-IPAD-001).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On Safari 18.2+ iPadOS, azimuth/altitude drive brush shape; on Safari 17 the app falls back to tilt with no error.
- [ ] Pencil hover shows a brush-size preview on supported iPads; mouse hover shows it everywhere.
- [ ] A note drawn on Safari iPadOS opens and renders identically on Chrome desktop (geometry parity).
- [ ] The app launches and takes a note on the min-bar Safari 17 (Tier 2 requirement).

## Technical notes
Extend the `dart:js_interop` PointerEvent reader ({{SN-WEB-004}}) to expose `altitudeAngle`/`azimuthAngle`; capability query, not a Safari version string check where avoidable. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §3 and `compatibility-matrix.md` §4 (Apple Pencil rows). CanvasKit renderer only on this surface.

## Security & privacy
Baseline (MASVS-PRIVACY-1): pencil coordinates/orientation are content and not logged; secure-context (HTTPS) required for coalesced/predicted reads. No new egress.

## UX notes
Editor canvas (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §7.2); hover preview matches the palette dock brush token. Best-effort banner is not needed, but document the Safari gaps in Settings > Handwriting & stylus help text. All 17 looks + dark; VoiceOver (Safari) canvas label preserved.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ink/test/web_safari_pencil_test.dart` (synthetic altitude/azimuth events, version fallback); manual Safari iPadOS smoke recorded in {{SN-WEB-023}} Tier 2.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-004.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs updated (web.md Safari notes) if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Implement OPFS + SQLite-WASM (drift) persistence in a Worker
body:
## Context
Local-first (decision 3) on web means the browser is the device store. The performance tier is **OPFS** (`navigator.storage.getDirectory()`) with **`createSyncAccessHandle()`** (Worker-only), which hosts **SQLite-WASM** (drift's web build) plus ink/PDF/audio blobs (`docs/platform/web.md` §4, ADR-0010 decision 3). This issue brings up drift-on-SQLite-WASM-over-OPFS in a dedicated Worker so the web app has a real local database matching the native drift schema ({{SN-CORE-004}}), not a toy store, and so note reads/writes never block the UI isolate.

## Scope
**In:** a Worker-hosted drift database on SQLite-WASM over OPFS sync access handles; the content-addressed blob store on OPFS files; schema/migration parity with the native drift store; parameterised queries only.
**Out:** persistence/eviction requests ({{SN-WEB-009}}), small prefs store ({{SN-WEB-011}}), cloud sync ({{SN-WEB-019}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A note written on web survives close → reopen byte-for-byte (round-trip through the Worker DB).
- [ ] All ink/PDF/audio blobs are content-addressed files under OPFS; the DB holds no raw blob bytes.
- [ ] DB access runs entirely in the Worker; the UI isolate never calls a sync access handle on the main thread.
- [ ] Chrome/Edge 86+, Firefox 111+, Safari 15.2+ all open the DB; on a browser lacking OPFS sync handles, the app degrades to an IndexedDB-backed drift store with a logged (no-PII) capability note.

## Technical notes
`packages/sane_core` repository interfaces implemented by a web storage adapter using `drift` web (`WasmDatabase`) + `sqlite3.wasm` over OPFS; blobs via `FileSystemSyncAccessHandle`. Use drift's parameterised query builder — never string-built SQL (CWE-89, checklist §9.1). Reference ADR-0010 decision 3 and `architecture/file-format.md`. Wrap all writes in try/catch for `QuotaExceededError`.

## Security & privacy
Note content stored encrypted before write where the crypto layer is present; OPFS is origin-private but NOT a security boundary against local malware — the crypto is (ADR-0010 Security impact). Controls: MASVS-STORAGE-1/2, parameterised queries (CWE-89). Never store keys in the DB or localStorage.

## UX notes
Invisible infrastructure, but a corrupt/failed DB open must surface a user-safe error (not a crash) on the Library screen (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §6) and offer 'reload'. All 17 looks + dark for that error card; screen-reader announced.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_core/test/web_drift_opfs_test.dart` (round-trip, migration, QuotaExceeded path) in headless Chromium; `app/integration_test/web_persistence_test.dart` (write/close/reopen parity).

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002, SN-CORE-004.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Guard web note durability with persist(), estimate() and eviction warnings
body:
## Context
Browser storage can be **evicted**: best-effort storage is LRU-evicted under disk pressure, and WebKit ITP evicts script-writable storage after **7 days without interaction** (`docs/platform/web.md` §4, ADR-0010 Context). This is a data-loss risk, so the web build MUST (a) request `navigator.storage.persist()` from a user gesture on first meaningful save, (b) check `estimate()` headroom and warn on low space, and (c) never treat OPFS/IndexedDB as the only copy — nudging the user toward cloud sync or install. This is a correctness requirement (p0, data-loss class), not a nicety.

## Scope
**In:** call `persist()` inside the save user-gesture; read `estimate()` and surface a low-space warning; an eviction-risk banner for un-synced guest notes nudging sign-in + cloud sync or PWA install; try/catch around all quota calls.
**Out:** the actual DB ({{SN-WEB-008}}), install prompt ({{SN-WEB-010}}), cloud sync engine ({{SN-WEB-019}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `navigator.storage.persist()` is requested from a real user gesture on the first note save; the granted/denied result is reflected in Settings > Sync & backup.
- [ ] When `estimate()` shows headroom below a threshold, a non-blocking low-space warning appears with a 'free up / sync' action.
- [ ] An un-synced web note shows an eviction-risk hint nudging sign-in/cloud-sync/install; a synced note does not.
- [ ] A simulated eviction loses no note that had been synced (durable copy recovers it); all quota calls are wrapped so `QuotaExceededError` degrades gracefully, never crashes.

## Technical notes
`dart:js_interop` to `navigator.storage.persist()/estimate()`; state via Riverpod in `app/`. Installed/Home-Screen PWAs are granted persistence heuristically — detect and skip the nag. Reference ADR-0010 decisions 3 and verify-step 4, and `docs/platform/web.md` §4 durability warning.

## Security & privacy
Eviction is an **availability/privacy** consideration, not confidentiality (data is encrypted at rest regardless) — MASVS-STORAGE-1, MASVS-PRIVACY-4 (data retention transparency). The warning copy must not expose file paths or content (checklist §7). No new egress; the sync nudge is opt-in.

## UX notes
Banner/toast on the Editor and Library screens (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §6/§7) and a status row in Settings > Sync & backup (§12). Calm, non-alarming copy (see §16 microcopy). All 17 looks + dark; dismissible; `Semantics` alert role; 44px targets.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_persistence_guard_test.dart` (persist gesture, estimate threshold, eviction-recovery via a synced copy); widget golden of the warning banner in two looks.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-008.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add Web App Manifest and installable PWA experience
body:
## Context
Installability is a web release gate (`docs/platform/web.md` §8): a valid Web App Manifest (name, icons, `display: standalone`, `start_url`, `scope`), a registered service worker, and an offline fallback. Chromium offers a rich install prompt via `beforeinstallprompt`; iOS/iPadOS Safari has **no** automatic prompt and requires manual **Add to Home Screen** (ADR-0010 Context). Installing unlocks better storage persistence, badging, push (iOS 16.4+) and file handling. This issue ships the manifest and a tasteful, platform-aware install affordance.

## Scope
**In:** the manifest with icon set and `standalone`/`scope`/`start_url`; a captured `beforeinstallprompt` custom install button on Chromium; an iOS A2HS instructions sheet; `launch_handler`/`client_mode` focus behaviour.
**Out:** the service worker/offline caching ({{SN-WEB-011}}), file handlers + share target ({{SN-WEB-012}}), badging ({{SN-WEB-012}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Lighthouse recognises the app as installable (valid manifest + SW registered) on Chrome desktop.
- [ ] Chromium shows the custom install button (from a stored `beforeinstallprompt`), not only the browser default; accepting installs the app.
- [ ] On iPadOS/iOS Safari, an A2HS help sheet explains manual install; the app runs in `standalone` once installed.
- [ ] Launching an already-open install focuses the existing window rather than opening a duplicate.

## Technical notes
`web/manifest.json` + icons (Sane Sage placeholder, design §9); capture `beforeinstallprompt` via `dart:js_interop` and defer it; `launch_handler: { client_mode: 'focus-existing' }`. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §5 and ADR-0010 decision 4 (progressive enhancement behind feature detection).

## Security & privacy
Baseline (MASVS-PLATFORM-3 secure defaults): manifest exposes no secrets; icons are first-party; no analytics on install. Install is user-initiated (no silent behaviour).

## UX notes
Install button placement per the Sidebar/free-plan card (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §2) and an Onboarding step (§5). iOS instructions sheet uses the Share-sheet iconography. All 17 looks + dark; button ≥ 44px, `Semantics` label 'Install Sane Notes'; dismiss is remembered (localStorage, per-viewer).

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_install_test.dart` (manifest validity, prompt capture/accept in headless Chromium); a golden of the install button + iOS sheet in two looks.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add service worker offline precache and runtime caching (Workbox)
body:
## Context
Full **offline note-taking** is a locked capability of the web surface, and a registered service worker is half of the installability gate (`docs/platform/web.md` §5/§8, ADR-0010 decision 4). The SW must precache the app shell + WASM runtime, serve an offline fallback, and use a safe runtime-caching strategy for versioned assets, while never caching sensitive responses. This issue replaces Flutter's default SW with a Workbox-based one tuned for the dual WASM/JS payload and aggressive caching to hit the < 3 s cached cold start.

## Scope
**In:** Workbox precache of the app shell, CanvasKit + skwasm WASM, fonts and icons; a runtime cache for same-origin static assets; an offline fallback route; SW update flow (skipWaiting + client reload prompt).
**Out:** file handlers/share target/badging ({{SN-WEB-012}}), OPFS DB ({{SN-WEB-008}}), CDN cache-control ({{SN-WEB-017}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the network offline, a previously loaded app cold-starts and lets the user open and edit a local note.
- [ ] Both the CanvasKit and skwasm runtime files are precached; a cached reload cold-starts in < 3 s on the reference desktop.
- [ ] An app update is detected and the user is offered a reload; stale caches are cleaned on activate.
- [ ] No API/auth/token responses are cached by the SW (allow-list is static assets only).

## Technical notes
Custom `web/sw.js` (Workbox `precacheAndRoute` + `registerRoute`); integrate with the manifest ({{SN-WEB-010}}). The SW script itself must be same-origin and covered by CSP; do not cache cross-origin auth or Drive responses. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §5 and ADR-0010 decision 4.

## Security & privacy
MASVS-STORAGE-1 (only non-sensitive static assets cached) and MASVS-PLATFORM-2 (SW is same-origin, integrity via versioned URLs). Never cache tokens, ciphertext blobs served from Drive, or note content responses (checklist §6/§8). SW served with `no-cache` so updates are not pinned.

## UX notes
An offline indicator on the Library/Editor chrome (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §6/§7) and an update toast (§16 microcopy, 2.4 s). All 17 looks + dark; `Semantics` status announcement for offline/online transitions; the update prompt is keyboard-reachable.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_offline_test.dart` (headless Chromium, offline app-shell load, note edit); a unit test of the cache allow-list; an SW-update flow test.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002, SN-WEB-010.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Register PWA file handlers, share target and app badging
body:
## Context
On capable browsers the installed PWA can behave like a native app: open `.sanenote`/`.pdf`/`.md` via `file_handlers` + `launchQueue.setConsumer` (Chromium desktop), receive shared files via a `share_target` POST (Chromium/Android), send shares via `navigator.share()`, and show an unread/sync badge via `navigator.setAppBadge()` (Chromium desktop; iOS 16.4+ installed). These are progressive enhancements behind feature detection (`docs/platform/web.md` §5, ADR-0010 decision 4). Because every inbound file is untrusted, this issue also enforces the input-validation checklist on the web import path.

## Scope
**In:** `file_handlers` for `.sanenote`/`.pdf`/`.md` + `launchQueue` consumer; `share_target` (`method: POST`, `multipart/form-data`) landing in a confirm/import view; `navigator.share()`/`canShare()` for export behind a user gesture; `setAppBadge()` for unread/sync.
**Out:** File System Access pickers ({{SN-WEB-013}}), the import parser internals (owned by SN-SHR/SN-PDF), sync badge source data ({{SN-WEB-019}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Opening a `.sanenote`/`.pdf`/`.md` with the installed app launches it and lands on an import **confirm** screen (never auto-imports/auto-mutates — checklist §1.1).
- [ ] A shared file arrives via `share_target` POST and reaches the same confirm view; oversized/wrong-MIME payloads are rejected with a user-safe error.
- [ ] Export uses `navigator.share()` only inside a user gesture; `canShare()` gates the UI on unsupported browsers.
- [ ] `setAppBadge()`/`clearAppBadge()` updates a count where supported and no-ops silently elsewhere.

## Technical notes
Manifest `file_handlers`/`share_target`; `dart:js_interop` for `launchQueue`, `navigator.share`, `setAppBadge`. Validate type/MIME (not extension), size caps, and schema before use; parse **off** the UI isolate; import into a **new isolated notebook** (checklist §1). Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §5 and secure-coding-checklist §1/§1.1.

## Security & privacy
Untrusted-input surface (MASVS-PLATFORM-1, OWASP-A08, CWE-434): cap resources before decode (zip/decompression bombs), canonicalise/confine paths, fail closed. Badge exposes only a count, never content (checklist §8). No auto-network on inbound file.

## UX notes
Inbound files use the Import PDF overlay pattern (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §9) and a generic Import confirm sheet; share uses the Share overlay (§10). All 17 looks + dark; confirm actions ≥ 44px, keyboard-reachable, `Semantics` described.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_file_handlers_test.dart` (launchQueue + share_target confirm flow, hostile-file rejection); a unit test of the MIME/size/schema validator; badge no-op test on an unsupported stub.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-010, SN-WEB-011.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Threat model row updated for the web import surface
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Implement File System Access open/save with browser-fs-access fallback
body:
## Context
Opening and saving real files (export a `.sanenote`/PDF, import a document) uses the **File System Access** `show*Picker()` API, which is **Chromium desktop only**; Safari/Firefox and all mobile browsers must fall back to `<input type=file>` for open and a download for save (the `browser-fs-access` ponyfill pattern), per `docs/platform/web.md` §4. This issue provides one capability-detected file-IO facade so the Library/Share flows work everywhere, with the native picker where available and the fallback elsewhere.

## Scope
**In:** a `WebFileIo` facade using `showOpenFilePicker`/`showSaveFilePicker` on Chromium and `<input type=file>` + download elsewhere; MIME/size validation on read; confinement of any content-derived path on write.
**Out:** `file_handlers`/share target ({{SN-WEB-012}}), OPFS internal store ({{SN-WEB-008}}), export format encoders (SN-SHR-001).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On Chromium desktop, save writes to a user-chosen file via `showSaveFilePicker`; open reads via `showOpenFilePicker`.
- [ ] On Safari/Firefox/mobile, save produces a download and open uses `<input type=file>`; both paths validate MIME + size before use.
- [ ] A malformed/oversized picked file fails closed into a user-safe error, parsed off the UI isolate.
- [ ] No write target is derived unsanitised from file content (no `..`, no absolute path, confined to the chosen handle) — CWE-22.

## Technical notes
`dart:js_interop` to File System Access; ponyfill behaviour hand-rolled (the artifact CDN allow-list forbids external libs at runtime — self-host or reimplement). Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §4 File-open/save row and secure-coding-checklist §1. Downloads are user-gesture-initiated.

## Security & privacy
MASVS-STORAGE-1, MASVS-PLATFORM-1, path-traversal defence (CWE-22, checklist §1): canonicalise/confine, reject symlinks/absolute paths; treat picked bytes as hostile. No silent disk access — every pick is user-initiated. No secrets written to disk.

## UX notes
Hooks the Share overlay export (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §10) and Library import. On non-Chromium, the UI copy says 'Download' rather than 'Save to…'. All 17 looks + dark; buttons ≥ 44px, keyboard-reachable, `Semantics` labelled.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_file_io_test.dart` (Chromium picker + fallback stub); a unit test of the MIME/size/path validator with hostile inputs; golden of the export sheet in two looks.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Threat model row updated if the file-IO surface changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md
